name: ClassRevision metadata is read-only and monotonically published

input.source_text: contract C { fun m() -> Nil } class A for C { public impl fun m() -> Nil { nil } } module Q { public fun run() -> Object { let origin = A.active_revision; let first = Reflection::Class.revision(A).fetch(:commit_id); let published = A.define_method(:extra) { 1 }; let second = Reflection::Class.revision(A).fetch(:commit_id); let failed = try { A.open() { |t| t.remove_contract(C) } } catch e { e }; let refused = try { Reflection::Class.reactivate(A, 1) } catch e { e }; [origin, A.active_revision, first == second, failed, refused] } } Q.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. C017's origin numbering is fixed: a Class DECLARATION is one publication, sealed into the origin revision, so a freshly declared Class reports 1. Verified by an_origin_class_declaration_publishes_revision_one and v959_revision_metadata_is_read_only_and_monotonic: failed candidates consume no number, and one successful publication takes one number and a distinct commit_id.
